coverage.main: Read all fourteen pages of arXiv 1811.02248v4 (CVPR 2019): Sections 1-5, Algorithms, Tables 1-3, Figures 1-9, references and supplementary Sections A-D (example images, perceptibility control, lambda effects Figures 14-16, comparison examples).
coverage.supplement: Supplementary Sections A-D are appended in the arXiv PDF and read. The CVF version was not retrieved.
coverage.excluded_results: Tables 1-2, Figure 6 and supplement Figures 14-16 attack each model directly (white-box); the adversarially trained ResNet-18 paragraph is white-box; Figures 1, 5, 7-13, 17-18 are qualitative. The 100% diagonal of Table 3 is the source itself.

result_groups.locator: Section 4.1 fooling-rate definition (p. 5); Section 4.2 'Transferability and semantic information' and Table 3 (pp. 7-8)
result_groups.population: 4,000 randomly selected ILSVRC2012 validation images; SparseFool perturbations from VGG-16, ResNet-101 and DenseNet-161 (PyTorch pretrained) fed to the other two models
result_groups.outcome: fooling rate: fraction of D whose target prediction changes from the target's own clean prediction k(x)
result_groups.evidence: Section 4.1 defines fooling rate as |{x in D : k(x + r_x) != k(x)}| / |D| over the full 4,000-image set D, with no clean-correct filter (targets have 71.6-77.7% clean accuracy in Table 2), so target-clean-incorrect inputs are explicitly included and the denominator does not depend on source success (the diagonal is 100%). The outcome is prediction change, not ground-truth misclassification; this estimand difference is recorded.

f1.evidence: Clean accuracy is reported separately for VGG-16 (71.59), ResNet-101 (77.37) and DenseNet-161 (77.65), every source and target in Table 3 (Inception-v3 also listed). The evaluation population of these accuracies is not stated.

f2.evidence: The fooling rate is defined over all images in D, including those the target misclassifies when clean. Explicit design choice, not missing reporting.

f3.evidence: The denominator is |D| with no source-success condition; SparseFool fooled every source image, so no failures needed exclusion. Coded no from the explicit population definition.

f4.evidence: One-decimal percentages over 4,000 images correspond to several possible integer numerators each (e.g., 10.8% -> 430-434).

f5.evidence: SparseFool minimizes the number of perturbed pixels (L1 relaxation of L0) with values bounded only by the image dynamic range; no L-infinity or L2 radius defines the attack. The optional +/- delta value bound is a perceptibility control studied separately. Explicit threat-model choice.

f6.evidence: The linked repository provides the SparseFool and DeepFool implementations and single-image test scripts; models are public PyTorch pretrained weights. The 4,000-image sample and a transfer-evaluation script are not released, so the Table 3 configuration cannot be identified without assumptions.

artifact_checks.result: Listed via the GitHub API (head 27 September 2020): sparsefool.py, deepfool.py, linear_solver.py, utils.py, test_sparsefool.py, test_perceptibility.py, two demo images and synset_words.txt. No transfer script or image list. Not executed.

bounds_checks.reason: The fooling rate counts changes from the target's own clean prediction, which is not the unconditional ground-truth misclassification probability in the bound; clean-correct/incorrect transitions cannot be separated from printed values. Not substituted.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. Coding fields 2/3 as explicit no relies on the formal fooling-rate definition applying to Table 3, which its caption supports.
